newsitem.title: UK: LME copper thwarted at $1,950 again, others flat.
newsitem.headline: LME copper thwarted at $1,950 again, others flat.

text.p: Copper prices eased in late inter-office trade on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Thursday after again failing to clear $1,950 resistance.
At 1800 GMT three month copper futures were quoted at $1,933/37 a tonne, below the post-kerb high of $1,947/51 and also below the afternoon kerb close of $1,944.
Traders said the market firmed in reaction to good warrant demand in Europe and tightening nearby spreads.
Cash/threes was indicated at a small backwardation after trading level during the afternoon ring sessions.
Dealers were looking for a sizeable stock drawdown early on Friday, but some said the price impact would be limited because the decline was already factored into the market.
But technically some dealers favoured the upside, with the next target above $1,950 pegged at around $2,000.
The October options declaration next Wednesday also supported the short term bullish price outlook, one trader said.
Other base metals were little changed from afternoon kerb closing levels by 1800 GMT.
